title: Sales Manager Salary: How to Convert Hourly Rates to Annual Pay
description: Learn how to calculate a sales manager salary from hourly rates using 38-hour weeks, award rates, casual loading, super, and tax. Fair Work and ABS data included.
salarySummary: A full-time sales manager earning the Commercial Sales Award rate of $29.55 per hour would have an annual salary of about $58,400 before tax and super, based on 38 ordinary hours per week.

faqs.q: What is the minimum hourly rate for a sales manager under the Commercial Sales Award?
faqs.a: Under the Commercial Sales Award 2020, the minimum hourly rate for a Commercial Traveller/Advertising Sales Representative (the classification most relevant to a sales manager) is $29.55 per hour for a full-time adult employee. This rate applies from 1 July 2026 and is set by the Fair Work Ombudsman. Casual employees receive an additional 25% loading, making the casual rate $36.94 per hour.

faqs.q: How do I calculate annual pay from an hourly sales manager rate?
faqs.a: Multiply the hourly rate by the number of ordinary hours worked per week (typically 38 for full-time) and then by 52 weeks. For example, $29.55 × 38 × 52 = $58,390.80 per year. This is a gross estimate and does not include overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. The same formula applies for casual rates, but remember the casual loading is already included in the hourly figure you use.

faqs.q: Does the National Minimum Wage apply to sales managers?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour (from 1 July 2026) applies only to employees not covered by an award or enterprise agreement. Most sales managers are covered by the Commercial Sales Award or a similar award, so the award rate takes precedence. If no award applies, the National Minimum Wage is the legal minimum.

bodyMarkdown:
## How to Convert a Sales Manager Salary from Hourly to Annual

Understanding your **sales manager salary** starts with knowing the correct hourly rate and how to convert it to annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures. Whether you are negotiating a new role or checking your current pay, the formula is straightforward: multiply your hourly rate by the number of ordinary hours worked per week, then by 52 weeks. For full-time employees, the standard is 38 hours per week under the Fair Work Act.

### Understanding the National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage each year. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour, or $1004.90 per week for 38 hours. However, most sales managers are covered by the **Commercial Sales Award 2020** [MA000083], which provides higher minimum rates. Under this award, a full-time Commercial Traveller/Advertising Sales Representative (the classification closest to a sales manager) earns $29.55 per hour, or $1122.80 per week. This is the minimum; many sales managers earn above the award through enterprise agreements or individual contracts.

If you are not covered by an award or agreement, the National Minimum Wage applies. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides pay guides for each award, including the Commercial Sales Award, which list all minimum rates, allowances, and penalty rates.

### The Role of Casual Loading

Casual employees in sales roles receive a 25% loading on top of the minimum hourly rate. For a Commercial Traveller under the award, the casual rate is $36.94 per hour (125% of $29.55). This loading compensates for the lack of paid leave entitlements such as annual leave and sick leave. When using our [timesheet](/), you can check a box to add the 25% casual loading to your base hourly rate. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading; the tool adds it automatically.

### Converting Hourly to Annual, Fortnightly, and Weekly

To calculate your annual gross pay:

**Annual = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a full-time sales manager on $29.55 per hour:
- Weekly: $29.55 × 38 = $1122.90
- Fortnightly: $1122.90 × 2 = $2245.80
- Annual: $1122.90 × 52 = $58,390.80

This assumes you work the same 38 ordinary hours every week with no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no allowances. If you work more than 38 hours, overtime rates (usually 150% for the first 3 hours and 200% thereafter) apply under the award.

### Superannuation and Tax Considerations

Superannuation is paid on top of your gross salary. The super guarantee rate is 12% of ordinary time earnings, up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year (2026–27). For a sales manager earning $58,390.80, the employer must contribute an additional $7006.90 to your super fund each year.

Tax is deducted using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income between $18,201 and $45,000
- 30% on income between $45,001 and $135,000
- 37% on income between $135,001 and $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (with reductions for low-income earners). For a $58,390.80 annual salary, the estimated tax (including Medicare) is approximately $8,500, leaving a take-home pay of about $49,900 per year. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide for a more detailed breakdown.

### Comparing with Average Earnings

The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports average weekly earnings for full-time adult employees in May 2026 at $2083.70 per week (ordinary time), which equates to about $54.83 per hour for 38 hours. This figure includes all occupations and is higher than the award rate for sales managers. Many sales managers earn above the award due to commissions, bonuses, or experience. Our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page provides more context.

### Using the Timesheet Tool

Our [timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate and see the annual, fortnightly, and weekly equivalents instantly. Remember to check the casual loading box only if you are a casual employee. The tool uses the same formula: hourly × hours per week × 52, with an option to adjust hours if you work a different pattern. It also estimates super and tax based on the latest rates.

### Key Takeaways

- The minimum **sales manager salary** under the Commercial Sales Award is $29.55 per hour for full-time employees.
- Casual sales managers receive $36.94 per hour including the 25% loading.
- Annual gross pay = hourly rate × 38 × 52.
- Super is 12% on top, and tax is calculated using the 2026–27 brackets plus Medicare.
- Always check the applicable award or agreement, as enterprise agreements may set different rates.

For more detailed information, refer to the [reference tables](/data) on our site, which include historical minimum wages and award classifications.
